components.css: .ds-strip{font-family: 'Schibsted Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;position:relative;max-width:640px;filter:drop-shadow(0 6px 10px rgb(28 30 29 / 0.12));transition:filter 600ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);}.ds-strip:hover,.ds-strip:focus-within{filter:drop-shadow(0 18px 22px rgb(28 30 29 / 0.24));}.ds-strip-paper{position:relative;min-height:96px;background:var(--color-paper, #fbfbf8);clip-path:polygon(0 50%, 28px 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 28px 100%);}.ds-stain{position:absolute;inset:0 auto 0 0;width:112px;background:radial-gradient(55% 130% at 100% 50%, transparent 60%, color-mix(in oklab, var(--hue) 68%, #3b2a1a) 63%, transparent 68%),linear-gradient(to right, color-mix(in oklab, var(--hue) 94%, white), color-mix(in oklab, var(--hue) 50%, white) 72%, transparent);opacity:.88;transition:opacity 600ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), filter 600ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);}.ds-strip:hover .ds-stain,.ds-strip:focus-within .ds-stain{opacity:1;filter:saturate(1.35);}.ds-strip-text{position:relative;display:flex;gap:24px;padding:16px 20px 16px 128px;}.ds-strip-main{flex:1;min-width:0;}.ds-strip-brand{margin:0;font-size:13px;color:var(--color-ink-3, #585c58);}.ds-strip h3{margin:2px 0 0;font-size:18px;font-weight:600;line-height:1.375;letter-spacing:-0.01em;}.ds-strip h3 a{color:var(--color-ink, #1c1e1d);text-decoration:none;}.ds-strip h3 a::after{content:"";position:absolute;inset:0;}.ds-strip h3 a:focus-visible{outline:none;}.ds-strip-notes{margin:4px 0 0;font-size:15px;color:var(--color-ink-2, #464a47);white-space:nowrap;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis;}.ds-figure{text-align:right;}.ds-figure div{font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;font-size:24px;font-weight:500;letter-spacing:-0.02em;color:var(--color-ink, #1c1e1d);}.ds-figure span{font-size:12px;color:var(--color-ink-3, #585c58);}

narrative.overview:
Every fragrance in Accord is a smelling strip (a mouillette) and the product is the bench a perfumer evaluates them on. The ground is a neutral bench grey; content sits on blotter-paper white cut into strips with die-cut tapered tips; each strip carries an oil stain in the one hue fixed to its Edwards wheel family, darkening to a tide line where the oil stopped soaking. Everything else is graphite ink. The world is light only, chosen from the use scene: perfume is judged on white paper in neutral daylight.

The system is quiet and typographic. One grotesk sets every word; a mono face appears only where a number or identifier has to be read exactly. There are no catalog images: the stain is the only picture a fragrance gets, and colour on a strip always means its accord family, never decoration. Depth is paper physics: strips rest with a soft drop shadow, lift and saturate when touched, and confirmed versus unconfirmed is carried by stained versus dashed blank paper.

Density is moderate. Pages run in one 1440px container with generous section breaks; lists are stacks of laid strips rather than grids of cards.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral bench grey ground, blotter-white paper strips with die-cut tapered tips.
One fixed stain hue per Edwards wheel family, with a darker tide line; unparsed accords stay unstained.
Graphite ink for text and primary actions; no brand accent colour.
Schibsted Grotesk for all text; Geist Mono only for ids, counts and figures.
Paper shadows and a lift-and-saturate response; no glass, no decorative gradients beyond the stain.

rules.name: The One Hue Per Family Rule
rules.body: A stain hue belongs to exactly one Edwards wheel family and is never reassigned, tinted for decoration or used for UI state. If a colour is on a strip, it names the accord.

rules.name: The Graphite Action Rule
rules.body: Actions are graphite ink on paper or bench. Do not introduce a brand accent for buttons or links; the stains are data, not chrome.

rules.name: The Instrument Mono Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono sets only ids (product ids), counts, percentages and match figures, always with tabular numerals. Words, names and headings are never mono.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Label Rule
rules.body: Small labels are sentence case at 13px in faint pencil, sitting directly above or beside the value they describe. No uppercase tracked labels.

rules.name: The Paper Physics Rule
rules.body: Only paper casts shadows, and only soft ones. No hard offset shadows, no glass or blur, no glow.

rules.name: The Lift and Saturate Rule
rules.body: Attention lifts paper and saturates the stain together (stain opacity 0.88 to 1, saturate 1.35); never one without the other on a stained strip.

rules.name: The Square Paper Rule
rules.body: Tags and chips are square paper at 2px. No pills.

dos: **Do** put every fragrance on a strip: laid strips for lists, standing strips for fans and detail pages.
**Do** stain a strip with its wheel family's fixed hue and leave unparsed accords unstained.
**Do** draw unconfirmed candidates as ghost strips (dashed, unstained) and keep confirmed answers stained.
**Do** set ids, counts and match figures in Geist Mono with tabular numerals, and everything else in Schibsted Grotesk.
**Do** keep tags as square paper (2px) and controls at 4px.
**Do** lift and saturate together on hover and focus, over 600ms on the paper ease-out, instant under reduced motion.
**Do** draw icons from the one 20px grid, 1.5px stroke, round-join set.
**Do** start strip text past the stain depth.
donts: **Don't** show catalog photos or bottle imagery; the stain is the fragrance's only picture.
**Don't** add a dark theme; the world is light only.
**Don't** use a stain hue for anything other than its accord family.
**Don't** use glass, blur, glow or decorative gradients; the stain is the only gradient.
**Don't** use hard offset shadows; paper shadows are soft.
**Don't** set names, headings or prose in Geist Mono.
**Don't** treat the strip mark in the nav and favicon as a final logo; it is a placeholder pending the owner's approval.
